newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-UNITED STATES CONTINUES SHUTOUT STREAK, BEAT TRINIDAD 2-0.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED STATES CONTINUES SHUTOUT STREAK, BEAT TRINIDAD 2-0.

text.p: The United States
recorded their sixth consecutive shutout in World Cup
qualifying and took sole possession of first place in their
CONCACAF group with a 2-0 win over Trinidad & Tobago Sunday.
Sweeper Thomas Dooley broke the scoreless tie in the 52nd
minute with a head ball after taking a cross from the right
side from Jeff Agoos.
Forward Eric Wynalda, off a feed from U.S. captain John
Harkes, fired a 25-metre blast past goalkeeper Haydon Thomas
for the clincher in the 84th minute.
It was the second victory in two matches for the United
States, who blanked Guatemala 2-0 last week in Washington,
D.C. The defeat virtually eliminated Trinidad (0-2-1), who
have lost and tied at home.
The last time the Americans conceded a goal in the
CONCACAF competition was in a 2-1 victory over Guatemala in
New Britain, Connecticut, on June 17, 1989.
Trinidad's best chance came in the 68th minute, when
Jerren Nixon (F.C. Zurich), got a step on defender Eddie Pope
and fired a shot wide right of goalkeeper Kasey Keller.
Keller, who will return to Leicester City of the English
Premier League this week, was hardly tested otherwise.
Trinidad will host the United States in a qualifier in
Port of Spain on November 24.
Teams:
United States: Keller; Dooley, Pope, Lalas, Agoos; Harkes,
Ramos, Renya, Stewart; Moore (Radsosavljevic, 56th), Wynalda
(Jones, 85th).
Trinidad & Tobago: Thomas; Faustin, Francis, Lee, Rougier;
Nakhid, Latapy, Eve (Dwarika, 16th, Thomas, 76th), Lewis
(Theodore, 56th); Nixon, Yorke.
